resale_co.name: Occupancy Permit (Certificate of Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Atlantic City Department of Licensing & Inspections
requirements: Certificate of Land Use (zoning) from Planning, (609) 347-5404, or the CRDA Tourism District, (609) 347-0500
Smoke certification from Fire Prevention (single-family or duplex)
Pest certification: report from a licensed exterminator that the unit is free of bed bugs, other insects and rodents
All utilities turned on for the inspection
No rubbish, debris or bulk garbage left on the property before the new occupancy
Buyer details (and all members or principals if the buyer is an LLC, corporation or partnership)
resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online with the City's GovPilot Occupancy Permit Application (choose the Sale application type, give the closing date and buyer details, and attach the Certificate of Land Use, smoke certification and pest certification). Questions go to the Licensing & Inspection Department, City Hall, 1301 Bacharach Blvd., 5th Floor, Suite 502.

evidence.quote: The owner of any residential property shall obtain an occupancy permit prior to the sale of such property involving a new occupancy of any unit of dwelling space, provided that no occupancy permit shall be required for the sale of vacant properties, but shall be required prior to such time as a new occupancy occurs.

If the buyer is an LLC, Corporation or Partnership, the following information must be included: individual names of all members of the LLC, principals of the corporation or partners in the partnership.
Smoke Certification (single-family or duplex only) Contact: Fire Prevention - City Hall - Room 130 (609) 347-5595
**Please Note that All UTILITIES MUST BE TURNED ON for an inspection to be performed.

resale_co.notes: The ordinance text comes from ecode360 search results only (the page itself cannot be opened); both phrases of the quote were confirmed by exact-phrase searches that returned the Atlantic City code page ecode360.com/15210509. The City's live GovPilot Occupancy Permit Application offers Rental, Sale and Reissue application types and asks for the closing date and buyer, which matches the ordinance. The fee is shown only after the online form is filled out, so no fee is recorded; search engine summaries of the City code mention permit and reinspection fees, but the exact words could not be confirmed. The City's posted inspection checklist ('To secure a Certificate of Occupancy', April 2026) is written for residential rental units (exterior items such as trip hazards, railings, roof, paint; interior items such as deadbolt, smoke and CO alarms, 2A10BC extinguisher, GFCI in bathrooms, working appliances, heat at 68 F from October 1 to May 1); it likely reflects what inspectors look at, but it is labeled for rentals. The form also mentions a Lead Safe certification with a $45 fee, but that is for rental units built before 1978. Landlord registration is a separate rental program. The City's contact data lists Sears Wright, MPA, as Assistant Director of Licensing & Inspections. No staff email was found. Re-checked 2026-10-06: the online Occupancy Permit form, the ordinance search results and the fire forms are unchanged; ecode360 pages and the City's law PDFs still could not be opened, so no Occupancy Permit fee could be confirmed.

requirements: Notarized owner affidavit (Smoke Certificate Affidavit) attached to the online application
10-year sealed battery smoke alarm on each level, including basements (not attic or crawl space)
Smoke alarm and CO alarm outside each separate sleeping area, within 10 feet of it
Existing AC-powered or interconnected alarms in homes built after January 1977 must be kept working
Portable fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 lb, on a hanger within 10 feet of the kitchen (2020 affidavit still lists it)

authorities.how_to_apply: Submit the City's online GovPilot Smoke Detector Application and attach the Smoke Certificate Affidavit, filled out and notarized. Pay by check to the City of Atlantic City, cash or money order. Fees are non-refundable and an inspection cannot be scheduled until payment is made. Office: City Hall, 1301 Bacharach Blvd, Room 130.

fire_cert.notes: Fees come from the Fire Prevention Bureau's Smoke Certificate Affidavit (PDF created July 2020); the online GovPilot form computes the fee only after it is filled out, so the current amounts could not be seen there. The affidavit says a new application is needed if the change of occupancy does not happen within 6 months, while the current online form says 90 days; the online form is newer. The 2020 affidavit names Mohammad R. Hatefi as Fire Official; the state fire directory (survey 1/27/2026) lists Kevin Munn, so the directory name is recorded. The online form links the affidavit at cityofatlanticcity.org; the same file is posted at acnj.gov. The affidavit still requires a portable fire extinguisher; the state law of February 3, 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19) removed it from the state requirement.
